title: HYG Database: named stars
blurb: The 450 brightest stars that have a proper name. One view is where each star really is in 3-D space around the Sun; the other is just where it appears on the sky, a perfect sphere. Neighbors on the sky can be hundreds of light-years apart.

about.name: HYG (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese) Database
about.quote: HYG combines every identifiable star in the HIPPARCOS, Yale Bright Star, and Gliese (nearby star) catalogs into a combined dataset of the stars' currently best-known positions, brightnesses, spectral types, and various additional catalog IDs such as traditional names and Bayer designations.
about.label: Astronomy Nexus (Codeberg)

here: Here: the 450 brightest HYG v4.1 stars that have a proper name (the Sun and four stars with unknown distance left out), as their 3-D position around the Sun with distance squashed to log10(1 + light-years) so a few far supergiants don't swamp everything (A), and as their direction on the sky, a point on a sphere (B).

hyg.text: Nash, D. (2024). The HYG Database, v4.1. Astronomy Nexus. CC BY-SA 4.0.
